4th Period.workingNow: Making your drawing code read the state variable instead of using a fixed size.
4th Period.weeklyDeliverable: week06-state-pattern.md in your Mario fork — a working small/big toggle plus a short write-up naming your states, your triggers, and what changes in each — committed by Sunday night.
4th Period.smartGoal: I can make my render code read my state variable so that changing the state changes what the player sees.
4th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.12 — Design and iteratively develop programs that combine control structures, including nested loops and compound conditionals.
4th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.6 — Reading closely and explaining how meaning is conveyed explicitly and implicitly through language.
agenda: I do: draw from the state, don't hardcode (8 min)
We do: find one hardcoded value together (5 min)
You do: make your render read the state (11 min)
Exit Ticket: one thing your state now controls (2 min)
4th Period.connections: Yesterday your key press flipped a variable. Today the rest of your code starts listening to it — that is what makes this a real state machine instead of two separate copies of Mario. Tomorrow you and a partner try to break each other's.

6th Period.workingNow: Playing your own game on purpose to find what breaks, and writing down three bugs.
6th Period.weeklyDeliverable: Your finished game, published from Code.org Game Lab and embedded on your Google Site with a one-paragraph description — link shared by Sunday night.
6th Period.smartGoal: I can test my game one part at a time so that I can find exactly what is broken instead of guessing.
6th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.17 — Systematically test and refine programs using a range of test cases.
6th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.5 — Listening actively to spoken English in a range of social and academic contexts.
agenda: Overview: today you test, not build (2 min)
I do: testing one thing at a time (6 min)
We do: test a shared game & name the bug (5 min)
You do: test your game, list 3 bugs (11 min)
Exit Ticket: your top bug to fix (3 min)
6th Period.connections: You have spent two days building. Today you stop adding and start testing — a game you have not broken on purpose is not finished. Tomorrow a classmate plays it and tells you whether it feels the way you planned back on your MDA sheet.
